newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NAB to arrange Eastern Energy cp issue.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NAB to arrange Eastern Energy cp issue.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd said on Tuesday it would arrange and manage a A$200 million domestic commercial paper programme for Eastern Energy Ltd.
NAB will all also act as issuing and paying agent.
The programme will enable Eastern, which is 100 percent owned by Texas Utilities Co, to issue commercial paper through a panel of dealers comprising NAB and three other financial institutions.
Eastern will use the proceeds for its general funding requirments. It acquired assets sold by the Victorian government in its recent privatisation process.
"The CP programme will diversify our funding sources and add flexibilty to our debt maturity profile," said Geoff Vincent, Chief Financial Officer at Eastern Energy.
Documentation is expected to be completed in mid-April with the first drawdown to be made shortly thereafter.
The programme is expected to be assigned a short term rating of A2 by Standard & Poor's.
NAB will also be providing a liquidity support facility to Eastern and participation in this may be syndicated to other financial institutions.

"Utilities represent a growing and important part of the Australian corporate debt market. This mandate is confirmation of National's commitment to Eastern and the utilities sector," said Peter Thomas, NAB General Manager, Wholesale Financial

NAB said that via its sales and distribution desk, it has observed a notable increase in demand for A-2 rated CP, reflecting a reduction in secondary market trading margins, and investor support for this sector is expected to continue to grow.
